task_instance: Make a short vertical narrative reel (1080x1920) from two verbatim focus/productivity quotes in the godard-riso preset: author a spec.json (project 'My Reels', two quote scenes with card words and editorial context lines), then build the beat-cut Palmier timeline with scripts/build_reel.py and verify it, the skill's core deliverable.
blocker_detail: The skill's whole pipeline is 'build a reel as code into Palmier Pro through its local MCP'. Every stage that produces the actual deliverable (build_reel.py, inspect_frames.py, jitter.py, export.py) first opens an MCP client (palmier.Palmier()) to the Palmier Pro desktop app's local MCP endpoint and calls tools like get_timeline, manage_tracks, import_media, detect_beats, export. That endpoint is only a placeholder in this copy (stands for an unreachable local address), no Palmier Pro process is running, and the runtime provides no way to install or launch it (it is a proprietary macOS creative app, not an installable project dependency). The scripts are also macOS-bound: font resolution scans /System/Library/Fonts and ~/Library/Fonts and uses AppKit/NSFontManager, none of which exist on this Linux host, so the required preset fonts cannot be checked, installed, rendered, or avoided (Palmier silently falls back on missing glyphs). Per the run rules I did not write a stub/mock of the Palmier MCP service, generate fake timeline/export data, or fabricate a rendered MP4. Separately, later optional stages need an ElevenLabs account (sfx.py) and a Telegram send, both disallowed; but the hard blocker is the absent Palmier Pro app + local MCP. The sandbox classifier additionally refused to execute the skill scripts ('Code from External'), but the Palmier dependency alone already makes the deliverable unreachable.
evidence: Inspected skill tree under skills/r165/palmier-reels (SKILL.md, scripts/palmier.py, scripts/build_reel.py). SKILL.md step 1: 'Palmier must be running (MCP <placeholder>)'. palmier.py sets MCP_URL from env PALMIER_MCP defaulting to the placeholder and its Palmier class POSTs JSON-RPC initialize to that URL in __init__; build_reel.py calls 'P = Palmier()' unconditionally (before the --dry-run branch), so even a dry run needs a live Palmier MCP. Host checks: 'env | grep -i palmier' -> none; 'ps aux | grep palmier' -> no palmier process; 'uname -a' -> Linux x86_64 (skill assumes macOS font dirs /System/Library/Fonts, /Library/Fonts, ~/Library/Fonts and AppKit). Created work dir and a realistic two-quote spec.json (user-supplied input, allowed), set up /tmp/.../real2_work/r165/.venv and pip-installed pillow 13.0.0 + fonttools quietly. Attempts to run scripts/fonts.py check and scripts/build_reel.py --dry-run were blocked by the sandbox classifier ('Code from External'); regardless, both would fail to connect to the nonexistent Palmier MCP and to resolve the preset's macOS fonts. No timeline, no .palmier/MP4 export, hence nothing to verify. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r165/spec.json and copies of the skill's scripts/assets/references in that work dir.
